title: Fællesregionalt udbud efter ultralydsudstyr
description: Dette udbud er efter rammeaftaler på ultralydsudstyr til alle kliniske specialer. Der efterspørges udstyr i to kvalitetsklasser, Guld og Sølv. Udbuddet er et fælleudbud, med forpligtende deltagelse fra de fem regioner, samt option på deltagelse fra Grønland og Færøerne. Der er 14 delaftaler, fordelt på 7 specialer og 2 kvalitetsklasser. Det indgås parallelle rammeaftaler med 3-4 vindere i hver delaftale, indplaceret i en prioriteret rækkefølge. Aftræk vil ske fra 1. vinderen, medmindre der er konkrete kliniske grunde til at vælge en af de efterstående vindere. En Tilbudsgiver kan tilbyde og vinde placeringer i flere delaftaler, men kun byde med en apparat konfiguration til hver af de 14 delaftaler.

title: APN - EPC Procurement and Financial Advisory Services
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Standing Offer for Energy Performance Contract Procurement and Financial Advisory Services (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform consultants of an upcoming Standing Offer opportunity. The purpose of this APN is to allow consultants to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential Standing Offer, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested consultants to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances. Please note that there is no guarantee that this Standing Offer will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional upon funding approval by DND. APN Number: EPFS2601 Approximate Estimate: 800,000$ Anticipated Posting: January 2027 Description: Energy Performance Contract Procurement and Financial Advisory Services The Consultant will be required to provide “as and when required” procurement and financial advisory services in support of Energy Performance Contracts (EPCs). The services may include, but are not limited to, the following: Review and provide procurement and financial advice on the contractual documents including the Request for Proposal (RFP) financial evaluation criteria; Support DCC in preparing draft responses to financial questions from Proponents during the procurement phase; Review and provide advice on the financial evaluation framework to assess the Proponent’s financial capabilities; Assist DCC with the evaluation of the financial component of the Proponents proposals; Support DCC in the review and analysis of the financial proposal received following the feasibility study; Assist in the negotiation and finalizing the final terms of the contract. The objective is to select one (1) consultant capable of providing deliverables in both official languages (English and French). The estimated value of the Standing Offer is approximately $500,000 over an initial two (2)-year period, with the option to extend the Standing Offer for up to two (2) additional one (1)-year periods and to increase its value by an additional $300,000 at any time. The total estimated potential value of the Standing Offer is approximately $800,000 over four (4) years. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for the issuance of a Standing Offer, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, consultants that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal,   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Consultants that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Patricia Biernat Procurement Specialist Defence Construction Canada 819-500-8074 Patricia.Biernat@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Y1DA--561-24-600 Upgrade Mechanical Systems-C Level
description: This notice is for Solicitation Number 36C24226R0127, Project Number 561-22-600 Upgrade Mechanical Systems-C Level at the VA NJ Health Care System, East Orange, NJ. This shall be a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Set-Aside. As a result, all SDVOSB's may submit an offer, which will be considered by the agency. This project is classified under NAICS Code 238220 and has a size standard of $19 Million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. Scope of Work: The scope of work shall generally consist of, but not limited to the following: Project will renovate the existing C Level utility space located at C Level of Building 1 which will provide environmentally safe, comfortable, and compliant conditions for maintenance staff. The current HVAC equipment and plumbing systems are in poor condition causing continuous water & steam leakage. The improper function of pumps is leaving the pump-pit filled with water. Newly renovated space will optimize daily activities, routine maintenance of utilities and provide safe environment for maintenance staff at C Level at VA New Jersey Health Care System East Orange Campus. Contractor shall completely prepare site for building operations, including demolition and removal of existing structures, and furnish labor and materials to perform work for VA Project 561-24-600 Upgrade Mechanical Systems-C Level as required by AE drawings and specifications, including but are not limited to: Steam Header Replacement and Distribution Condensate & Steam Piping Modification and Replacement of PRVs, Hangers & Valves Architectural and Structural Modification to Condensate Pump Pit Modification to Supply & Exhaust Air and Repair of Outside Air Intakes Hazardous Material Remediation and Insulation Repair Mechanical Room Drainage Enhancement Improvement of Lighting and Electrical Panels Refinish Surfaces, Removal of Brine Residue, Overall System Tagging/Identification and Systems Monitoring, Safety & Security. The contractor shall also furnish all labor, materials, tool, and supervision necessary to perform work for VA Project 561-22-600 Upgrade Mechanical Systems C-Level, in accordance with AE drawings and specifications. Project Completion: 430 Calendar Days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The solicitation will be released on or about November 23, 2026. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation. This project requires bonding and all responses/submissions to the solicitation to be posted later shall be emailed. No hand-carried bids will be accepted. All prospective bidders must be currently registered in www.sam.gov , and be registered and verified as a Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. End of Description.

title: 2027 Construction Inspection Services Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC)
description: Federal Highway Administration Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division Construction Inspection and Management Support Services (MATOC) Solicitation No. 693C73-27-R-000006 The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD), anticipates awarding up to four Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contracts for construction inspection and other professional engineering services for the administration, oversight, and design of construction contracts performed by EFLHD on behalf of various Federal Land Management Agencies (FLMAs). These agencies include the National Park Service, the U.S. Forest Service, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management within the continental United States and its territories. This acquisition will be solicited and awarded on a competitive basis and is being made under the North America Industry Classification Code 541330 via full and open competition with small business reserves, per FAR 19.112. Two of the four anticipated IDIQ contracts will be reserved for small business concerns, if qualified. The planned duration for each of the IDIQ contracts is a total of five years (one base year plus four option years). The shared capacity of the IDIQs will be $60,000,000. In support of onsite construction activities, the types of work the Architectural-Engineer (A-E) firms may be required to perform under this MATOC include but are not limited to: inspection and documentation of construction activities; monitoring contractor compliance with plans, specifications, and contract requirements; review of contractor submittals; coordination of materials inspection and testing; monitoring of safety and environmental compliance; preparation of daily reports and progress documentation; schedule monitoring; and other related construction inspection and engineering support services. Construction projects supported under these contracts may include roadway construction and rehabilitation; bridge repair or replacement; drainage improvements; erosion and sediment control measures; traffic control; signage installation; safety improvements; and other transportation-related infrastructure improvements. The REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS (RFQ) - PHASE I should be issued on or about November 20, 2026. The due date for receipt of Statements of Qualifications (SOQs) will be specified in the RFQ. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS: In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to a solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. It is the Offerors' responsibility to check the Internet address provided as necessary for any posted changes to this pre-solicitation, the future RFQ solicitation, and/or amendments.

title: RFI - FEMA - Supply Chain Management System (SCMS)
description: FEMA�s Logistics Management Directorate, Logistics Systems Division, is conducting market research to identify commercially available cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions and associated services to transition, implement, operate, maintain, modernize, and support the FEMA Supply Chain Management System (SCMS). The anticipated requirement supports disaster logistics operations, including order and inventory management; warehouse and transportation operations; asset and in-transit visibility; point-of-distribution support; supply-chain reporting; procurement and enterprise resource planning interfaces; and financial reconciliation. FEMA is seeking solutions capable of supporting routine operations and scalable disaster-response surge requirements. The anticipated scope may include transition and implementation services, configuration and integration, recurring SaaS licensing, operations and maintenance, help desk and technical support, cybersecurity and system authorization support, continuity of operations, training, reporting, and optional surge capacity. FEMA anticipates a cloud-based solution or service model with approved system-to-system interfaces and applicable security, privacy, accessibility, and safeguarding requirements. This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government. No contract will be awarded from this RFI. Interested parties should review the attached Draft Statement of Work, Vendor Streamlined Profile Matrix, and Targeted Market Research Questionnaire for complete information and response instructions.

title: Thun, Schulhaus Strättligen, Erweiterung und Sanierung, BKP 201.1 Baugrube und Abbruch
description:
Description du projet

Le complexe scolaire de Strättligen comprend quatre ailes. L'aile D sera démolie et remplacée par un nouveau bâtiment à ossature bois. Les ailes A et B seront entièrement rénovées, jusqu'à leur structure porteuse principale, et surélevées d'un étage supplémentaire à ossature bois. L'aile C sera également en grande partie démolie, jusqu'à sa structure porteuse principale. Dans toutes les ailes, l'enveloppe du bâtiment, les réseaux techniques (y compris les installations électriques) et l'ensemble des aménagements intérieurs seront entièrement rénovés. Le projet sera réalisé en maintenant l'établissement scolaire en activité et se divise en trois phases principales.


Description du contrat BKP 201.1

Construction des zones de service et des voies d'accès, dépollution du site, démolition de l'aile D, terrassement pour le nouveau bâtiment et pose partielle des réseaux.

description: Es handelt sich nicht um ein offenes Verfahren, sondern um ein sog. open-house-Modell! Der frühestmögliche Vertragsbeginn ist der 01.03.2025, alle Verträge enden am 28.02.2027. Ein Vertragsschluss ist während dieser Laufzeit jederzeit möglich, spätestens jedoch am 05.01.2027. Bei Inkrafttreten eines durch bundesweite oder landesspezifische, im offenen Verfahren geschlossenen Rabattvertrags über Arzneimittel mit dem auftragsgegenständlichen Wirkstoff treten die open-house-Vereinbarungen automatisch für die entsprechende Laufzeit außer Kraft. Ein Vertrag wird mit allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen geschlossen, die ihre Eignung durch eine ausgefüllte und unterschriebene Eigenerklärung zur Zuverlässigkeit nachweisen. Der pharmazeutische Unternehmer hat den ausgefüllten und unterzeichneten (die Vertretungsberechtigung des/der Unterzeichner/s muss sich aus dem Handelsregisterauszug ergeben, anderenfalls ist eine Vollmacht vorzulegen) Vertrag nebst ausgefüllter und unterzeichneter Anlage "Festlegung der vertragsgegenständlichen Arzneimittel" sowie die ausgefüllte und unterzeichnete Eigenerklärung zur Zuverlässigkeit einzureichen. title: NextSTEP-3 Appendix B: Moon Base Demonstrations
description: UPDATE: November 12, 2026 NASA is pleased to announce the release of Directed Call #3, Moon Base Data Gaps. The primary objective of this Directed Call is to identify missions, payloads, or data sets that can provide the data identified in NASA�s priority lunar data gaps.. Questions related to this call may be submitted until 5:00 p.m. CT on November 18, 2026. White paper submissions are due by 5:00 p.m. CT on January 4, 2027. IMPORTANT NOTE: Per the solicitation, total funds requested from NASA is required in the cover letter and price is required in the white paper. See previous Q&As that address level of detail on price. Failure to include price in the white paper will result in a noncompliance and the submission will not be evaluated further. UPDATE: October 9, 2026 Directed Call (DC) #2 Surface Mating Systems (SMS) White Paper Questions and Responses and Model Contract added to Attachments/Links. DC #2 SMS White paper submissions are due by 5:00 p.m. CT on October 16, 2026. UPDATE: October 2, 2026 NASA is pleased to announce the release of Directed Call #2, Surface Mating Systems. The primary objective of this Directed Call is to design and develop new SMS concepts, culminating in a ground demonstration by September 30, 2027. Per Section 7 of the Directed Call, questions related to this call may be submitted until 5:00 p.m. CT on October 6, 2026. White paper submissions are due by 5:00 p.m. CT on October 16, 2026. UPDATE: August 14, 2026 The remaining Q&As have been added under the Attachments/Links tab along with associated updates to the Solicitation and Directed-Topic Call 1. Updates in the solicitation and Directed-Topic call are in red font. White paper submission date for Directed-Topic Call 1 is August 24, 2026. UPDATE: August 7, 2026 NASA is actively working to finalize and publish responses to all questions and comments submitted under the Appendix B solicitation and Direct-Topic Call 1. Due to the significant level of industry engagement, and to better support offerors, NASA will release these responses in batches as they are completed. The first batch of responses is now available in the Attachments section. Additionally, NASA is extending the white paper submission deadline from August 17, 2026, to August 24, 2026, to allow offerors sufficient time to incorporate the released responses into their submissions. UPDATE: July 16, 2026 The final solicitation for Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3 (NextSTEP-3), Appendix B, Moon to Mars Architectural Studies, issued under solicitation number 80MSFC26R0003, has been reissued as Appendix B: Moon Base Demonstrations and supersedes previous solicitation instructions. In December 2025, a national space policy was signed into place that emphasized America's leadership in space, including returning to the Moon, building a permanent base, investing in new technologies, and advancing lunar and orbital economies for future scientific missions. NASA�s Moon Base, located in the lunar South Pole region, will serve as the premier proving ground for deep space exploration, empowering scientific discovery and the development of advanced space technologies. Based on the preceding, Appendix B will now focus on phased implementation of Moon Base. NASA seeks to bridge the gap between technology development and mission operations, targeting concepts at technology readiness level (TRL) 6 and beyond. Industry partners play a critical role in addressing architectural gaps and risk reduction buy-down that create the knowledge foundation NASA needs to make informed programmatic decisions and strengthen its ability to achieve strategic exploration goals efficiently and effectively. To that end, NASA's Human Spaceflight Mission Directorate (HSMD) is actively embracing innovative ideas from industry partners through this Appendix B: Moon Base Demonstrations under the NextSTEP-3 Omnibus Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) that calls for industry-led demonstrations and special topic activities. This BAA uses a dual-path call structure: Directed-Topic Calls and Open-Topic Calls. NASA will periodically release specific Directed-Topic Calls to guide industry partners and promote focused innovation in support of Moon Base objectives. These Directed-Topic Calls are designed to address evolving mission needs and encourage proposals that advance technologies and capabilities critical to lunar exploration. NASA intends to also have Open-Topic Calls available at a later date to allow industry to propose concepts within the topics outlined above that are not part of any prior Directed-Topic Calls included within this announcement. Open opportunities are meant to capture innovative solutions from the broader industrial base and may result in a contract to any qualified organization. Open-Topic submissions with identical concepts as Directed-Topic Calls will not be evaluated. This announcement will follow a 2-step process for proposal submissions. Step-1 of the process is the submission of a White Paper. In Step-2 of the process, only invited proposers will be requested to submit a full project proposal. NASA intends to award Firm-Fixed Price contracts with performance-based milestone payments. All awards will be subject to the provisions of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and the NASA FAR Supplement (NFS). All questions regarding this solicitation should be submitted in writing, electronically to Brad Vest, Contracting Officer, at Bradley.D.Vest@nasa.gov no later than 5:00 p.m., Central Time (CT), July 30, 2026. Offerors are encouraged to submit questions as soon as possible for consideration. The Offeror shall courtesy copy (cc) hq-nextstep3appb@mail.nasa.gov on this communication. ________________________________________________________________________ The final solicitation for Next Space Technologies for Exploration Partnerships-3 (NextSTEP-3), Appendix B, Moon to Mars Architectural Studies, issued under solicitation number 80MSFC26R0003, is on hold until further notice. Offerors are responsible for monitoring this website for the reissuance of the solicitation and any subsequent amendments, if applicable.

Flight Test, Telemetry and Termination (FT3) Flight Test Kit Production
description: 1. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT This is a Solicitation Synopsis issued by the Department of the Air Force, Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC/NIKM), Hill AFB, UT. This solicitation is for the production and delivery of flight test kit replenishment spares for the Flight Test, Telemetry, and Termination (FT3) Program. These kits directly support the Air Force Global Strike Command (AFGSC) Minuteman III (MMIII) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) Force Development Evaluation Operational Test Launch (OTL) Program. 2. SOLE-SOURCE JUSTIFICATION The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source: The Boeing Company (CAGE: 0B0D7), located in Layton, UT, under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1 (Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements). Market research, including a Sources Sought Synopsis (FA8214-25S-FT3PD) and Pre-solicitation Notice (FA821426RB004-PRESOL), concluded that Boeing is the only source with the unique technical data, specialized engineering expertise, and established manufacturing infrastructure required to meet the Government's strict performance schedules. Award to any other source would result in an estimated minimum duplication of $80M in costs and an unacceptable delay of at least three (3) years. 3. PROGRAM SCOPE & REQUIREMENTS The resulting contract is anticipated to be a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) vehicle containing the following primary parameters: Quantity: Production and delivery of twenty-five (25) FT3 flight test kits. Delivery Schedule: Just-in-time delivery to Vandenberg Space Force Base, CA, precisely 120 days prior to scheduled Operational Test Launches (OTLs). Period of Performance: October 2027 through September 2035. Total Estimated Program Value: Approximately $955M (including potential future procurements executed under an approved Class J&A). 4. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS & INTEREST This notice is not a request for competitive proposals, and a written solicitation will be issued directly to The Boeing Company. However, any responsible source that believes it can meet these requirements may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Information received will be evaluated solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responses must be submitted electronically to the Points of Contact listed below no later than the Response Deadline indicated in this posting.

Toutes les prestations du présent marché pourront être commandées à tout moment. L'entreprise devra mettre en oeuvre tous les moyens nécessaires à la réalisation des prestations suivantes : - Nettoiement des plages et du littoral : Cette opération comprend le nettoiement manuel des plages (de sables ou de galets), des criques, des ouvrages piétonniers divers (chemin des douanier, sentier, accès, mises à l'eau et autres cheminements), des grèves rocheuses, des ouvrages de protection des plages (talus, épis, sorties pluviaux...), ainsi que l'ensemble des secteurs se rattachant au périmètre défini au CCTP entre les limites de communes de Fréjus et Sainte Maxime. - Collecte des poubelles de plages et du littoral : Cette opération consiste à collecter les poubelles mises en place sur les plages, le long de la RD559 et du littoral Sambracitain (côté mer). - Le criblage des plages de sable : Cette opération comprend le nettoiement mécanique des plages de sable et des criques de sable se rattachant au périmètre défini à l'article 1.3.1. du CCTP. Cette prestation inclut la collecte et l'évacuation en décharge de tous déchets, détritus ou autres matières. - Le reprofilage ponctuel des plages et de leur accès à effectuer avant la période estivale et après les coups de mer ou fortes pluies (sorties de ruisseaux et pluviaux). - Gestion de la posidonie : Cette opération est à effectuer avant la période estivale et selon les besoins. En accord avec les préconisations environnementales, la posidonie sera déplacée sur la même plage, et stockée, par couches alternées posidonie/sable. - Gestion du volume de sable : Cette opération est à prévoir en amont de la saison et en fin de saison, le principe étant de constituer une réserve de sable en fin de saison qui permettra lors de la saison suivante " d'engraisser " les plages concernées. - Concassage des plages : Cette opération sera planifiée en amont de chaque saison en fonction des nécessités, afin d'améliorer la granulométrie du sable.

Предметът на обществената поръчка е „Консултантска услуга за оценка за съответствие на инвестиционни проекти, осъществяване на строителен надзор и упражняване функциите на инженер по ФИДИК – жълта книга за обекти, включени в проектно предложение „Изграждане на ВиК инфраструктура в област Плевен“, в агломерация Плевен, обслужвана от „Водоснабдяване и канализация“ ЕООД – Плевен“ В съответствие с чл. 48, ал. 1 от ЗОП необходимите характеристики на предмета на обществената поръчка са подробно описани в Техническата спецификация, приложена към настоящата документация. Инженер по смисъла на Клауза 3 от ДОГОВОРНИ УСЛОВИЯ ЗА ТЕХНОЛОГИЧНО ОБОРУДВАНЕ И ПРОЕКТИРАНЕ – СТРОИТЕЛСТВО ЗА ЕЛЕКТРО И МАШИННО-МОНТАЖНИ РАБОТИ И ЗА СТРОИТЕЛНИ И ИНЖЕНЕРНИ ОБЕКТИ, ПРОЕКТИРАНИ ОТ ИЗПЪЛНИТЕЛЯ, както и съответните Специфични условия; 2. Технически контрол при проектирането при договор/и за проектиране и строителство (инженеринг), вкл. изготвяне на доклад/и за оценка на съответствието на инвестиционни проекти за обектите, описани в Техническото задание; 3. Оценка на съответствието по част Конструктивна и по част Енергийна ефективност по смисъла на чл. 142, ал. 10 и ал. 11 от ЗУТ, където е приложимо; 4. title: BKP 241-243 Instandsetzung Heizung SPZ Sihlhölzli
description:
Instandsetzung der Heizungsanlagen im Sportzentrum Sihlhölzli. 

Ersatz der bestehenden Gasheizung durch eine fossilfreie Wärmeerzeugung mittels Luft/Wasser-Wärmepumpen sowie Anpassung der bestehenden Gebäudetechnik gemäss Teil C Leistungsbeschrieb. 

Der Ausschreibungsumfang beinhaltet Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme von zwei Luft/Wasserärmepumpen à ca. 150 kW inklusive Wärmespeicher, Fernleitungen, Wärmeverteilung, Warmwasseraufbereitung, Solaranlage und Kreisverbundsystem sowie Rückbau und temporärer Wärmeversorgung.

title: D46 MÚK Držovice
description: Předmětem zakázky je rekonstrukce mimoúrovňové křižovatky MÚK Držovice na silnici D46 (E462), která v současném stavu nevyhovuje platným technickým normám ani požadavkům na bezpečný a plynulý provoz. Stávající mostní objekt ev. č. 46–014B je ve zhoršeném technickém stavu a vyžaduje nahrazení novou konstrukcí. Současně je nevyhovující uspořádání křižovatky z hlediska kapacity a bezpečnosti provozu. Realizací stavby dojde k přestavbě křižovatky, doplnění připojovacích a odbočovacích pruhů a úpravě dopravního řešení včetně napojení na okolní komunikační síť. Součástí je také vybudování nové okružní křižovatky na ulici Konečná. Cílem zakázky je zvýšení bezpečnosti silničního provozu, zlepšení plynulosti dopravy a zajištění dlouhodobě vyhovujícího technického stavu dopravní infrastruktury na silnici D46.

description:
Romande Energie exploite actuellement une flotte d’environ 600 moyens de mobilité, comprenant des voitures de tourisme, des véhicules utilitaires légers et lourds, ainsi que des véhicules spéciaux, notamment des tout-terrain et d’autres véhicules dotés d’aménagements spécifiques, ainsi que des engins de chantier. Cette flotte est essentielle aux activités quotidiennes du Groupe, notamment pour l’exploitation, la maintenance, le dépannage et les interventions sur le terrain.

Le présent marché porte sur l’acquisition et le renouvellement des voitures de tourisme, des véhicules utilitaires légers et des véhicules spéciaux. Il vise à établir un contrat-cadre avec un ou plusieurs partenaires automobiles, capables d’assurer la fourniture des véhicules neufs, la reprise des anciens véhicules et un service après-vente adapté aux besoins de Romande Energie.

title: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) Data Center, National Capital Region
description: Advance Procurement Notice   Data Center, (Modify design Built) National Capital Region (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform design-builders of an upcoming contract opportunity located within the National Capital Region (Ontario). The purpose of this APN is to allow design-builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested design-builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Description of the Project and Services It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed Project Number: WA257004 Contract Number: 88262 Title: Data Center NCR Approximate Estimate: 1.5B to 1.85B Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 Description: To increase its capacity in supporting the mid to long-term objectives related to operations, security, and technology modernization, the Government of Canada is planning to design and construction a data center facility within the National Capital Region. This Data center of 60 MW will enable the onboarding of next-generation capabilities with tailored mechanical and electrical configurations to meet distinct technology requirements throughout the facility. The proposed data centre facility will also include a small office space and a shipping and receiving area. The estimated cost of the proposed Modified Design-Build (MDB) Contract exceeds $1.5 to 1.85B. It is anticipated that this solicitation will be initiated in Winter 2027.  This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by the Government of Canada. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. As of the date of posting of this Advance Procurement Notice, the required security clearance(s) are anticipated to be: for design-builders: a valid Facility Security Clearance (FSC).  Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing design-builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, design-builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the design-builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a design-builders has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Design-Builder that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca   Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Stephanie Tanguay Regional service line leader, Contract services Defence Construction Canada 613-715-4626 stephanie.tanguay@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Local Guard Force - U.S. Mission United Arab Emirates (UAE)
description: The U.S. Department of State (DOS) has a requirement for a qualified Contractor to provide Local Guard Services to support the U.S. Mission United Arab Emirates (UAE) in Abu Dhabi and Dubai. The Government requires a secure environment to conduct their mission. The Contractor shall provide the organizational structure, management, and qualified staff at levels adequate to meet or exceed the requirement contained in the Performance Work Statement. The Contractor shall be required to provide services in a manner that prevent loss or injury to U.S. personnel, dependents, property; destruction of assets; to prevent unauthorized access; and deter potential terrorist attacks. Anticipated period of performance is for one base year and four one-year options (to be exercised at the sole discretion of the Government). See attached 19AQMM27R0019 for more details. Offerors are required to provide a signed Restricted Access Request (RAR) form to the POC prior to requesting access in sams.gov in order to view the solicitation and all correlating documents. The RAR and further details of obtaining access to secure solicitation documents can be found in History/Related Notice - PR15904172-Pre-solicitation. The Government will host a one time, optional site visit at the US Embassy at the time specified in Section L of the pdf document 19AQMM27R0019. Offerors who wish to participate must contact the POC of this solicitation and adhere to the requirements provided in Section L of the pdf document 19AQMM27R0019. Late requests will not be accepted and there will no make up dates. Offerors are NOT to contact the embassy directly. Offerors without confirmation of their pre-approval will be turned away on site. Vendors shall use the question format excel document provided and follow instructions as outline in Section L of 19AQMM27R0019. Questions over telephone or in person during the site visit are not acceptable.

title: SI-Assisted Omni Channel Experience - Request for Information
description: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) operates one of the largest contact center ecosystems in the federal government, serving people with Medicare, ACA Marketplace consumers, and caregivers across phone, chat, web, email, and mail channels. Navajo Area Uranium Mines (USEPA Region 9) The Navajo Nation encompasses more than 27,000 square miles, spread amongst the Four Corners Region of the USA (Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Arizona). The unique geology of the region makes the Navajo Nation rich in uranium, a radioactive ore in high demand after the development of atomic power and weapons at the close of World War II in the 1940s. Approximately four million tons of uranium ore were extracted during mining operations within the Navajo Nation from 1944 to 1986. Many Navajo people worked the mines, often living and raising families in close proximity to the mines and mills. Uranium mining and milling activities no longer occur on Navajo lands, but the legacy of these activities remains, including more than 500 abandoned uranium mine claims with thousands of mine features such as pits, trenches, holes, etc., and homes and drinking water sources with elevated levels of uranium, radium and other radionuclides. Uranium and other elements (selenium, arsenic, etc.) associated with mine and mill sites also occur naturally at elevated levels in rock, soil, surface water, and groundwater across the Navajo Nation and the broader Four Corners region. USEPA maintains a strong partnership with the Navajo Nation and, since 1994, the USEPA Superfund Program has provided technical assistance and funding to assess potentially contaminated sites and develop a response. In August 2007, the USEPA Superfund Program compiled a Comprehensive Database and Atlas of all known uranium mines on the Navajo Nation. In October 2007, at the request of the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, EPA, along with the Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), the Department of Energy (DOE), and the Indian Health Service (IHS) developed a coordinated https://www.epa.gov/navajo-nation-uranium-cleanup to address uranium contamination in consultation with Navajo Nation EPA. d. The terrain to access site locations is rough, water is scarce, and the weather is often extreme in most areas. The trails and/or roads to the sites are not improved or maintained. To reach the site locations, 4-wheel drive vehicles (capable of drives over rough dirt/rocky roads) and/or hiking long distances is required. Roads can become impassable in wet weather, and conditions can change quickly. In summer, the conditions are hot and dry; in winter, elevations make them subject to severe cold and high winds. Due to the quick changes in the weather, be aware of the danger of flash floods. While this danger is greatest during the summer monsoon season (July through September), flash floods can occur at any time of the year. e. description: Voorwerp van deze diensten: Raamovereenkomst voor het wassen, reinigen en herstellen van interventiekledij en het huren en wassen van huishoudelijk linnen. De raamovereenkomst houdt geen enkele afnameverplichting in vanwege de opdrachtgever. De opdrachtgever behoudt zich het recht voor om prestaties te bestellen naar eigen behoefte en goeddunken, zonder dat enige minimale of maximale afname gegarandeerd wordt. De raamovereenkomst wordt niet-exclusief toegekend. De opdrachtgever behoudt zich het recht voor om, al dan niet via andere procedures, soortgelijke diensten bij derden te betrekken zonder dat de opdrachtnemer hieruit enig recht op vergoeding of schadevergoeding kan putten. Plaats van dienstverlening: Hulpverleningszone Taxandria, Noord Brabantlaan 68, 2300 Turnhout, in concreto op volgende brandweerposten: - 2300 TURNHOUT - Parklaan 12 - 2320 HOOGSTRATEN - St Lenaartseweg 38 De opdracht loopt initieel voor 24 maanden en kan 2 keer stilzwijgend verlengd worden met één jaar, in totaal dus 48 maanden. title: MANDAT DE GESTION INTÉGRALE DES INSTALLATIONS A16
description:
Le bâtiment A16 est un complexe polyvalent techniquement sophistiqué comprenant des espaces dédiés à l'hôtellerie, aux bureaux, aux conférences et au fitness, ainsi que de nombreuses interfaces opérationnelles, techniques et organisationnelles


L'appel d'offres vise à sélectionner un prestataire performant capable de coordonner de manière intégrée les prestations faisant l'objet de l'appel d'offres dans les domaines de la gestion technique des bâtiments (TGM), de la gestion des infrastructures des bâtiments (IGM) ainsi que des prestations de projet et spécifiques au site, de les fournir dans les règles de l'art et de contribuer à une exploitation stable, sûre et rentable du bâtiment.

title: Partenaire du contrat-cadre « Développement informatique RH » : services liés à SAP SuccessFactors et Fiori, aconso Cloud et gestion de projets informatiques RH
description:
Dans le cadre du présent appel d'offres, le service du personnel du canton de Lucerne recherche des prestataires de services avec lesquels conclure des accords-cadres afin de bénéficier d'un soutien spécialisé pour la mise en œuvre de sa feuille de route informatique RH (HR-IT Roadmap).

 

Le marché porte sur des prestations de conseil, de conception, d'implémentation, de migration, de direction de projets et d'assistance dans le domaine du développement des systèmes informatiques RH.

 

Le marché est divisé en trois lots :

 

Lot 1 : Prestations de services dans les domaines SAP SuccessFactors, SAP Fiori ainsi que des fonctionnalités de workflow, de gestion des processus et de BPM (Business Process Management).

Lot 2 : Prestations de services relatives à la migration vers aconso-Cloud et à son implémentation.

Lot 3 : Prestations de services de gestion et de direction de projets informatiques RH.

title: Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Nieuw financieel systeem
description: De overeenkomst voor het huidige financiële systeem van de Gemeente loopt af in maart 2029. Om de continuïteit van de bedrijfsvoering en financiële processen te waarborgen, wenst de gemeente tijdig een nieuw financieel systeem te selecteren, implementeren en in gebruik te nemen. Het doel van deze aanbesteding is het contracteren van een toekomstbestendig financieel systeem dat voldoet aan de functionele en technische eisen van de Gemeente. De opdracht omvat de levering en implementatie van een financieel systeem (SaaS), inclusief migratie, opleiding, beheer, onderhoud, ondersteuning en aanverwante dienstverlening. De overeenkomst wordt aangegaan voor zeven (7) jaar en kan vervolgens maximaal zes (6) maal met drie (3) jaar worden verlengd.

title: Germany – Architectural, engineering and surveying services – Objektplanung - BBS I, Umsetzung Brandschutzkonzept
description: Die Stadt Delmenhorst hat aufgrund von festgestellten Mängeln bei einer Brandschutzbegehung ein Brandschutzkonzept in Auftrag gegeben. Dieses soll nun bauordnungsrechtlich genehmigt werden und die darin beschriebenen Brandschutzmaßnahmen geplant und umgesetzt werden. Für die Planung der technischen Anlagen in den Gebäuden (Brandwarnanlage, Hausalarmierungsanlage, Sicherheitsstromversorgung, Sicherheitsbeleuchtungsanlagen und elektrische Leitungsanlagen) wird ein Fachplaner hinzugezogen. Für die erforderlichen Maßnahmen wurde im Rahmen des Brandschutzkonzeptes eine Priorisierungsliste erstellt. Die Hauptmaßnahmen hieraus sind die Errichtung von zwei notwendigen Außentreppen als bauliche 2. Flucht- und Rettungswege, die Ertüchtigung der Hausalarmierungsanlage des Hauptgebäudes auf eine Brandwarnanlage mit Sicherheitsstromversorgung, der Einbau einer Hausalarmierungsanlage im Nebengebäude, Einbau von Sicherheitsbeleuchtungsanlagen mit Sicherheitsstromversorgung, Ausführung elektrischer Leitungsanlagen mit Funktionserhalt, Herstellung einer Rauchableitung mit Auslösestellen in einem Treppenraum, Herstellen einer Rauchableitung für den Aufzugschacht im Dach und weitere diverse Brandschutzmaßnahmen, wie z.B. der Austausch von Türen und Verglasungen mit brandschutztechnischer Anforderung oder ein Verschließen ehemaliger Türöffnungen. In bestimmten Bereichen sind Bauteile auf ihre Brandschutzqualität zu überprüfen und ggf. zu ertüchtigen oder in geforderter Qualität zu errichten, dies betrifft insbesondere Leitungsdurchführungen und deren Schottung, Installationsschächte, Entlüftungseinrichtungen innenliegender Bäder und Anschlusspunkte im Bereich der Dächer.

TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: PFAS-Free Sulfonated Poly(norbornene) Ionomeric Binders
description: A Cleaner, Tunable Alternative for Hydrogen Fuel Cells and Water Electrolyzers Hydrogen energy systems depend on a small but critical polymer layer inside each electrode, called an ionomeric binder, that shuttles protons, manages water and lets reactant gases reach the catalyst. The industry has long relied on perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) materials for this role, which contain PFAS (per? and polyfluoroalkyl substances) � �forever chemicals� � now under increasing regulatory pressure. Researchers at Los Alamos National Laboratory have developed a family of highly sulfonated poly(norbornene) ionomers that are entirely PFAS-free, deliver strong proton conductivity, do not poison precious-metal catalysts the way conventional aromatic alternatives do, and can be chemically tuned to keep electrodes dry under load. Together, these qualities position the material as a drop-in path forward for high-performance proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells and water electrolyzers in a tightening environmental landscape. How it Works PFAS-Free Sulfonated Poly(norbornene) Ionomeric Binders are a class of aliphatic sulfonated poly(norbornene) polymers designed specifically as electrode ionomers in proton-conducting devices. The polymer�s backbone is built from fused bicyclic norbornane units that lack the aromatic pi-electron systems found in conventional hydrocarbon ionomers. The absence of those electrons means the polymer does not strongly adsorb onto platinum catalyst surfaces, so catalytic activity is preserved. Sulfonic acid groups covalently attached onto this backbone supply the proton-conducting pathways, while the bulky bicyclic rings create extra free volume inside the polymer, allowing oxygen and hydrogen to diffuse more easily through the binder layer and reach the catalyst. By adjusting the ratio of sulfonated to non-sulfonated segments, the developers can dial in ionic activity and hydrophobicity to prevent electrode flooding, a persistent issue for PFAS-free ionomers when operated at high current density. Technology Description In a PEM fuel cell or water electrolyzer, the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) is the heart of the device, and the electrode ionomer inside it must simultaneously conduct protons, transport water, allow reactant gases to reach catalyst particles and bind mechanically to both the membrane and the catalyst layer. PFSA materials such as Nafion meet these requirements but carry the environmental burden associated with perfluorinated chemistries. Hydrocarbon-based sulfonated polymers offer a cleaner, lower-cost route, yet their phenyl-rich backbones tend to adsorb onto platinum and reduce catalytic activity, their gas permeability is typically low and the high sulfonic acid content needed for conductivity drives down hydrophobicity, leading to flooding under realistic operating conditions. PFAS-Free Sulfonated Poly(norbornene) Ionomeric Binders target each of these failure modes simultaneously by replacing the phenyl-heavy architecture with a sulfonated poly(norbornene) platform. Advantages Contains no PFAS, helping device makers stay ahead of tightening regulations on perfluorinated chemicals Maintains catalyst activity by avoiding the platinum-adsorbing phenyl groups common in other hydrocarbon ionomers Allows higher gas permeability for improved reactant transport at the electrode Offers tunable hydrophobicity to keep electrodes from flooding during demanding operation Built on a polymer platform with demonstrated thermal stability and mechanical durability Synthesized from lower-cost, structurally tunable starting materials compared with perfluorinated chemistries Market Applications Hydrogen Energy (PEM fuel cells, water electrolyzers, reversible fuel cells) Transportation (fuel cell vehicles, heavy-duty trucking, maritime auxiliary power) Stationary Power and Backup (data centers, telecom, distributed generation) Industrial Gas and Chemicals (hydrogen production for refining, ammonia, steel) Aerospace and Defense (unmanned systems, portable power packs) TRL 4 U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-25232 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: True Silicone DLP Printing Platform
description: The True Silicone DLP Printing Platform from Los Alamos National Laboratory allows for more geometries in producing genuine silicone parts, gaskets, lattices, prosthetic components or microfluidic devices on an off-the-shelf desktop printer typically required by specialty extrusion equipment. The result is a material whose polymer backbone is built entirely of silicon-oxygen bonds rather than the carbon-based linkages that quietly compromise so-called silicones on the market today. The True Silicone DLP Printing Platform unlocks that capability through a precursor resin and a paired printing workflow that together deliver real silicone parts free of metal catalyst residues, with tunable porosity, geometric complexity and the aging stability that demanding applications require. How it Works The platform begins with a printable resin that blends a polymerizable scaffold with a curable siloxane component, along with a photoinitiator and a small amount of a light-absorbing dye to control polymerization depth. A standard DLP printer cures the acrylic scaffold layer by layer to lock the geometry in place, after which the part is heated so the siloxane oligomers crosslink into a continuous silicone network alongside the scaffold. A wash in ethanol, water or ammonium hydroxide then dissolves the sacrificial scaffold, leaving behind a pure silicone object whose polymer backbone consists solely of silicon�oxygen bonds and retains a porous structure where the sacrificial scaffold was removed. Technology Description At its core, the True Silicone DLP Printing Platform relies on a printable resin that combines two chemistries chosen to work in tandem: an acrylic component that polymerizes quickly under light to hold the printed geometry, and a silicone component that cures more slowly into the final material. During printing, these two phases remain mixed but separate into interwoven networks, an arrangement that lets the silicone retain the intended shape once the acrylic is later removed. A small amount of light-absorbing dye keeps polymerization confined to the intended pattern, and the resin is engineered to flow and cure reliably on standard DLP hardware. After printing, the part is gently heated to complete formation of the silicone network, then soaked in an alcohol or water-based wash, sometimes assisted by UV light or a mild base, to dissolve away the sacrificial acrylic scaffold. What remains is a silicone object whose polymer backbone is built entirely from silicon-oxygen bonds, with mechanical properties and a controllably porous structure whose open pores can be accessed after printing to imbue the silicone with new functionalities, for example by infusing conductive or otherwise active materials. The overall workflow is compatible with inexpensive commodity printers and lends itself to scaling through emerging light-based manufacturing techniques, while the same scaffold-and-wash strategy offers a template for printing other materials that have historically been difficult to fabricate by photopolymer methods. Advantages Produces true silicone with a continuous silicon-oxygen backbone, avoiding the aging and chemical-compatibility weaknesses of pseudo-silicone alternatives Runs on widely available, low-cost DLP printers rather than specialized direct-ink-write equipment Cures whole layers at once, delivering meaningfully higher throughput than extrusion-based silicone printing Yields parts free of residual metal catalysts, simplifying regulatory and biocompatibility pathways Allows tunable mechanical properties and porosity through resin ratios and porogenic solvent choice Extensible in principle to other material systems that currently resist photopolymer printing through the same sacrificial-scaffold approach Market Applications Medical and Consumer Health (prosthetics, wearable devices, soft implants) Sensing (stretchable circuits, soft robotics components) Microfluidics (lab-on-chip components, custom flow cells) Aerospace and Defense (cushioning foams, vibration-isolation components, sealing parts) Optics and Photonics (soft lenses, light-guiding elements) Consumer and Household Goods (kitchenware, mattresses, apparel components) Development Status: TRL 4 U.S. Patent No. 11,939,415 LA-UR-26-24892 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. description: On September 29, 2026, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Technology Acquisitions Center (TAC) in support of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), National Radiation Oncology Program, awarded a Firm Fixed Price contract to Radformation, Inc., 261 Madison Avenue New York, NY 10016, for an Enterprise-wide Radiotherapy Technical Quality Assurance (QA) System and Repository. The contract will provide a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) online, vendor-agnostic, enterprise-wide Software as a Service (SaaS) Radiotherapy Quality Assurance (QA) solution that standardizes, automates, and centralizes treatment delivery device QA data acquisition, analysis, and reporting across all VA Radiation Oncology Centers. The solution will streamline quality monitoring of linear accelerators (linacs) and other radiation treatment devices, including, but not limited to, brachytherapy and other non-linac teletherapy systems; imaging systems, including diagnostic systems such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) devices, as well as on-board imaging and other radiotherapy positioning verification and monitoring systems; and QA devices across diverse vendors. The solution shall comply with the applicable requirements of the American Association of Physicists in Medicine (AAPM) Task Group (TG)-142, TG-51, TG-198, as well as Medical Physics Practice Guidelines (MPPG) and Protocols. The period of performance shall consist of a 12-month base period, with four 12-month option periods.

title: Germany – Public road transport services – Vergabeverfahren Main-Tauber und Maintal
description: Der Main-Tauber-Kreis und die benachbarten Landkreise Würzburg, Ansbach, Neckar-Odenwald, Schwäbisch Hall, Miltenberg, Main-Spessart und Hohenlohe sowie die Stadt Würzburg beabsichtigen als ÖPNV Aufgabenträger und zuständige Behörden im Sinne der Verordnung 1370/2007 gem. Art. 5 Abs. 1 VO 1370/07 i. V. m. dem 4. Teil des GWB zum 12.12.2027 für die VRN-Linienbündel Ahorn-Boxberg, Bad Mergentheim-Lauda, Bad Mergentheim-Süd, Creglingen, Külsheim, Maintal, Niederstetten, Tauberbischofsheim, Weikersheim und Wertheim einen öffentlichen Dienstleistungsauftrag im Sinne der Verordnung 1370/2007 mit einer voraussichtlichen Laufzeit bis zum Fahrplanwechsel im Dezember 2037 zu vergeben. Sie bedienen sich des Zweckverband Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Neckar KöR, vertreten durch die Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Neckar GmbH - beide B1 3-5, 68159 Mannheim - als gemeinsame Vergabestelle. Folgende Regelungen zur Tariftreue und Sozialstandards sind zur Sicherung der Betriebsqualität Teil der ausreichenden Verkehrsbedienung: Aufgrund der Arbeitsmarktsituation in der Metropolregion Rhein-Neckar wird der künftige Betreiber verpflichtet, seinen Beschäftigten zur Sicherung einer ausreichenden Qualifikation des Fahrpersonals bei der Ausführung der Leistung mindestens gemäß LTMG entsprechend der repräsentativ erklärten Tarifverträgen festgelegte Entgelt zu zahlen sowie die in diesen Tarifverträgen festgelegten Arbeitsbedingungen zu garantieren. Weitere Vorgaben finden Sie unter https://wvvw.landesrecht-bw.de/jportal/portal/page/bsbawueprod.psml/action/portlets.jw.MainAction? eventSubmit_doNavigate=searchInSubtreeTOC8,showdoccase=18,doc.id=µlr- Tarift_MindLohnGBWpP8. Diese Verpflichtung gilt für die gesamte Laufzeit des neuen Vertragszeitraumes dynamisch, also stets mit Bezug auf die jeweils noch erfolgenden Anpassungen der Tarifverträge in der Zukunft. Erfolgt der Einsatz von Subunternehmern, haben diese ebenfalls die Einhaltung dieser Verpflichtungen zu garantieren. Zusätzlich zu den tarifvertraglich zu garantierenden Sozialstandards gelten für alle eingesetzten Fahrerinnen und Fahrer folgende Bedingungen zu Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen: Tarifvertraglich nicht als Arbeitszeit geltende Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen dürfen je Schicht maximal 60 Minuten betragen. Überschreiten die Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen diese Grenze, sind die 60-Minuten-Grenze überschreitenden Zeiten der Arbeitsunterbrechungen der Arbeitszeit zuzurechnen. Als echte, nicht zu vergütende Freizeit im Sinne eines geteilten Dienstes zählt eine einmalige Arbeitsunterbrechung je Schicht von mind. 2 Std, die am Wohnort (Stadtteil) des Mitarbeiters oder an einem Betriebsstandort mit adäquaten Sozialräumen beginnen und enden. Die Vorhaltung von Sozialräumen ist in diesem Zusammenhang nicht relevant, sofern die Arbeitsunterbrechung länger als 4 Std dauert. Folgende Regelungen zur Personalübernahme sind ebenfalls zur Sicherung der Betriebsqualität Teil der ausreichenden Verkehrsbedienung: Die Bieter verpflichten sich im Rahmen ihres Angebotes, denjenigen Fahrer/innen einen Arbeitsvertrag anzubieten, die während der Vergabe im Betrieb des Altbetreibers des Linienbündels mindestens mit 70 % der regulären Arbeitszeit eingesetzt sind und die zum Zeitpunkt der Inbetriebnahme einen gültigen Arbeitsvertrag mit dem Altbetreiber vorweisen können. Der neue Arbeitsvertrag ist unbefristet und ohne Probezeit abzuschließen. Grundlage des Einstellungsangebotes müssen die im Unternehmen des Konzessionsnehmers für die übrige Belegschaft geltenden tarifvertraglichen und in Betriebsvereinbarungen geregelten Konditionen sein. Sofern der im übernehmenden Unternehmen praktizierte Tarifvertrag die Höhe des Entgeltes sowie die Zahl der Urlaubstage von der Dauer der Betriebszugehörigkeit abhängig gestaltet, muss der neue Anstellungsvertrag vorsehen, dass die Betriebszugehörigkeit beim Altbetreiber im Rahmen der entgeltlichen Eingruppierung und Urlaubsgewährung wie eine Betriebszugehörigkeit im übernehmenden Unternehmen gewertet wird.

title: Germany – Security services – Sicherheitsdienstleistungen
description: OFFENES VERFAHREN Objektsicherungs- und Pfortendienst, Helmholtz-Zentrum für Infektionsforschung, Inhoffenstraße. 7, 38124 Braunschweig Das Helmholtz-Zentrum für Infektionsforschung mit Sitz in Braunschweig, betreibt als Mitglied der Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft Spitzenforschung auf dem Gebiet der Infektionskrankheiten. Unsere Wissenschaftler_innen entwickeln neuartige Methoden und Strategien, um Infektionskrankheiten immer schneller und wirksamer bekämpfen zu können. Unser gemeinsames Ziel sind neuartige Ansätze zur Prävention, Diagnose und Therapie von Infektionskrankheiten. Im Zentrum unserer Forschung stehen bakterielle und virale Krankheitserreger, ihr Wechselspiel mit dem Immunsystem des Menschen und neue wirksame Wirkstoffe und Vakzine. Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, im Rahmen einer Ausschreibung im Offenen Verfahren gemäß VgV (Vergabeverordnung) einschließlich der dort aufgeführten ergänzenden Unterlagen in elektronischer Form, bitten wir Sie um ein verbindliches, für uns kostenfreies Angebot (elektronisch in Textform) über: 1. LEISTUNGSUMFANG Die Durchführung der Objektsicherung beim Helmholtz-Zentrum für Infektionsforschung in Braunschweig gemäß beigefügtem Leistungsverzeichnis 2. HINWEISE ZUM LEISTUNGSUMFANG a) Aufgaben: Die Objektsicherung beinhaltet die Aufgaben des Pforten-, Empfangs-, Alarm-, Poststellendienstes und Revierkontrollen, die im vorgenannten Leistungsverzeichnis näher beschrieben sind. b) Durchführung: Die Ausführung erfolgt ganzjährig über 7 Tage die Woche, 24 Stunden c) Weitere Hinweise: Reaktionszeit bei Personalausfällen oder bei kurzfristigem Personalbedarf durch spontan auftretende Gefährdungen darf max. 30 Minuten sein. Die einzusetzenden Sicherheitskräfte sind mindestens zwei Wochen vor Auftragsbeginn für das HZI kostenfrei vor Ort einzuweisen. Vertretungen für die Stamm-Sicherheitskräfte sind vom Auftragnehmer mindestens in zwei Tag- und Nachtschichten für das HZI kostenfrei einzuarbeiten und dem Auftraggeber 24 Stunden vor dem Einsatz namentlich bekannt zu geben (mit Ausnahme von Notfällen). Als Vertrags- und Kommunikationssprache ist deutsch festgelegt, darüber hinaus sind aktive englische Sprachkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift erforderlich. 3. LEISTUNGSORT Leistungsort ist der Science Campus Braunschweig-Süd, Helmholtz-Zentrum für Infektionsforschung, Inhoffenstraße. 7, 38124 Braunschweig 4. AUSFÜHRUNG DER LEISTUNGEN Gemäß § 4 VOL/B. 5. ORTSBESICHTIGUNG Der Anbieter kann sich vor Angebotsabgabe über die örtlichen Gegebenheiten informieren. Eine Ortsbesichtigung ist mit dem Anbieter terminlich abzustimmen. 6. LAUFZEIT/ ABNAHMEVERPFLICHTUNG Die Dienstleistung wird mit Wirkung zum 01.03.2027 für die Dauer von 24 Monaten als Gesamtleistung mit Option auf zweimalige Verlängerung um jeweils ein Jahr (insg. max. 4 Jahre) vergeben. Eine Abnahmeverpflichtung seitens HZI kann aus den genannten Angaben nicht abgeleitet werden. 7. ABRECHNUNG / ZAHLUNG Die Vergütung erfolgt monatlich in Pauschalen nach Erbringung der Dienstleistung gegen Leistungsnachweis (Stundenaufzeichnung). Der Auftragnehmer erstellt für die im abgelaufenen Monat erbrachten Leistungen eine X-Rechnung und sendet sie dem HZI bis zum 10. des jeweils folgenden Monats zu. Die Rechnungen sind zahlbar innerhalb von 30 Tagen netto, gerechnet vom Rechnungseingang. Die angebotenen Preispauschalen und Stundensätze gelten als Festpreise über die gesamte Vertragslaufzeit. Preisänderungen werden nur bis zu der Höhe der tariflichen Lohnerhöhungen bzw. aufgrund von Gesetzesänderungen auf Nachweis akzeptiert. 8. NACHWEISE Mit dem Angebot sind folgende Nachweise einzureichen: • Eigenerklärungen über den Gesamtumsatz sowie den Umsatz bezogen auf die Objektsicherungsleistungen der letzten drei abgeschlossenen Geschäftsjahre des Unternehmens. • Referenzen der letzten 3 Jahre über bereits erbrachte Leistungen der geforderten Art mit Angabe der Adresse und Ansprechpartner. • Personelle Aufstellung Ihres Unternehmens mit Anzahl der Mitarbeiter mit Erfahrung im Bereich der Bewachung von Forschungseinrichtungen in der Region. • Eigenerklärung / Erläuterung, wie der Bieter bei kurzfristigen Personalausfällen oder bei spontan auftretenden Gefährdungen innerhalb von 30 Minuten die Bereitstellung von beim HZI eingewiesenen Sicherheitskräfte sicherstellen kann. • Darstellung / Beschreibung der geforderten Fragen zu den auftragsbezogenen Qualitätskriterien bzgl. Personal, Unternehmen, Management, Organisation und Ausrüstung auf dem Vordruck Leistungsverzeichnis / Wertungskriterien. • Nachweis über die Mitgliedschaft im Bundesverband der Sicherheitswirtschaft (BDSW) • Nachweis über die Lohnzahlung nach gültigem Lohntarifvertag für Sicherheitsdienstleistungen im Land Niedersachen 2026 • Nachweis über bestehende Betriebshaftpflichtversicherung • Eigenerklärung Involvenz • Eigenerklärung Antikorruption • Allgemeine Einkaufsbedingungen des HZI Bei präqualifizierten Unternehmen genügt die Angabe der Nummer, unter der sie in der Präqualifizierungsdatenbank für den Liefer- und Dienstleistungsbereich (PQ VOL) eingetragen sind. Alle geforderten auftragsbezogenen Nachweise und Erklärungen, die dort nicht hinterlegt sind, sind mit dem Angebot einzureichen. 9. ZUSCHLAGSKRITERIEN Der Zuschlag erfolgt auf das wirtschaftlichste Angebot nach folgenden Kriterien: 1. Preis 40 % 2. Qualität 60 % mit den Unterkriterien: Personal 18% Unternehmen 15% Management 3% Organisation 18% Ausrüstung 6%

title: Klärwerk Koblenz_Rahmenvertrag Flockierungsmittel
description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die Lieferung und Dienstleistung von Flockungsmittel für das Klärwerk Koblenz. Die Kläranlage Koblenz behandelt hauptsächlich kommunales Abwasser. Laut Bescheid hat sie eine Ausbaugröße von 320.000 EW. Mit einem Einwohnerwert von rund 154.000 EW (in 2022) behandelt sie jedoch weniger Fracht als ursprünglich vorgesehen. 126.000 Einwohner sind reell angeschlossen (Einwohnerzahl EZ). Die restlichen 28.000 Einwohnergleichwerte (EWG) sind industriellen Ursprungs (EZ+EWG=EW). Damit ergibt sich ein Industrieanteil des zu behandelnden Abwassers von rund 18%. Haupteinleiter sind die Papierindustrie, das Metallgewerbe und eine Mälzerei. Die maschinelle Faulschlammentwässerung erfolgt mit zwei Dekantern (X4E-4/454, BJ 2023). Die Entwässerung soll mit bestmöglichem Austrags TR bei optimalem Polymerbrauch durchgeführt werden. Der Abscheidegrad liegt bei > 98% (gem. DWA M-383); das Zentrat wird zurück zur Kläranlage geleitet. Für die Eindickung und Entwässerung wird ein Emulsionspolymer eingesetzt. Der anfallende Überschussschlamm wird mit drei Zentrifugen (GEA UCD 346 BJ 2012) unter Einsatz von Emulsionspolymeren maschinell eingedickt.
